lessons: Start with curiosity-driven paradoxes or counter-intuitive statements (e.g., cars crushing to save lives, T. rex inability to run), as all videos maintain over 1.0 retention at 10% regardless of initial comparative performance.
Avoid dry physics definitions or multi-sentence premise setups early on, as drops occur heavily between 11% and 25% when explanations become overly technical.
Keep comparisons relatable and fast-paced; physical analogies like car weights and tooth pressure hold audience attention better than abstract metrics.
Not enough data to definitively link countdown formats to retention patterns, as all evaluated videos have countdown set to false.
Maintain high narrative momentum past the 50% mark; videos with sharper mid-point drop-offs struggle to retain audiences through the ending.
worst_moment_types: Technical weight and muscle mechanics explanations that slow down the narrative pace
Multi-step scientific extrapolations involving complex bone and force calculations without immediate visual payoffs
best_hook_types: Immediate size or speed comparisons involving everyday objects like cars
Hypothetical survival scenarios placing the viewer directly in the shoes of the subject (e.g., imagining being a baby T. rex)
